title: Finance showcase catalog
description: The A2UI v1.0 catalog of the Somnio x Google finance showcase: one component per projection family, plus Section. GENERATED from the projection registry — do not edit by hand. Regenerate with: cd backend && make catalog
instructions:
Views the client can draw. You do not choose one and you never write a view id, an options object or JSON in your answer: a surface is attached by the tool you call, and your lever is which tool you call and which arguments you give it. Read this catalog to know what a tool's arguments can produce, then answer in plain prose about what the reader is seeing. An unknown view, an undeclared option or an out-of-range value is rejected and the default view is rendered instead. Never invent a payload shape, a field or a formatted number.
- activity.timeline.v1 — The Activity tab: the ledger as a timeline grouped under today, this week and each month, filtered by kind, every row captioned and its amount signed the way the design colours it.
  options: query (string of up to 24 characters, or omit it), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), kind (one of 'all', 'buy', 'sell', 'staking_reward', 'deposit'), limit (integer 1..200)
- attribution.driver.v1 — One holding's part in today's move: its contribution, the price move behind it, the units that carried it and its share of the day's result. The card a tapped waterfall bar opens.
  options: locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), symbol (one of 'AAVE', 'ARB', 'AVAX', 'BTC', 'ETH', 'LINK', 'SOL', 'USDC')
- attribution.waterfall.v1 — Unrealised profit and loss walked from cost basis to market value, one bucket per holding, biggest move first.
  options: fields (list of up to 8 (text), or omit it), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD')
  use when: the user asks WHY a value changed and the answer decomposes into signed contributions that sum to a net delta — what drove the portfolio's result, profit and loss by position. The steps arrive largest move first; do not reorder them.
  do not use for: a static breakdown of what is held now — `holdings.allocation.v1` answers that. Never write the figures yourself: render this view and copy the `display` strings it returns.
- attribution.window.v1 — The portfolio's move over a chosen window, one bucket per holding, biggest mover first. Not unrealised profit and loss: this compares each holding to what it was worth when the window opened, not to what it cost.
  options: fields (list of up to 8 (text), or omit it), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), window (string matching ^(1d|7d|30d)$)
- holdings.allocation.v1 — Allocation of the portfolio's market value — by holding, asset class or sector — with weight and day change per slice, the count in the donut's centre, and the all-time gain under the total.
  options: top_n (integer 1..20), include_other (true or false), sort (one of 'value_desc', 'value_asc', 'label'), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), group_by (one of 'holding', 'asset_class', 'sector'), headline (true or false)
- holdings.positions.v1 — The Holdings tab: total value with the all-time gain, then one row per position — units and average cost, value, unrealised result, today's move, price and weight — each with the question that hands it to the assistant.
  options: query (string of up to 24 characters, or omit it), sort (one of 'value_desc', 'value_asc', 'label'), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), asset_class (one of 'all', 'layer1', 'layer2', 'stablecoin', 'defi', 'infrastructure')
- order.ticket.v1 — Order ticket: a proposed buy or sell with its units, entry price and notional, plus the bounded inputs that re-render it. It places nothing.
  options: locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), symbol (one of 'AAVE', 'ARB', 'AVAX', 'BTC', 'ETH', 'LINK', 'SOL', 'USDC'), side (one of 'buy', 'sell'), size (string matching ^[0-9]{1,9}(\.[0-9]{1,8})?$), size_in (one of 'units', 'usd')
- order.ticket.v2 — Multi-leg draft order: each leg struck at its reference price with its weight in the order, the order's impact — total, fees, cash remaining, the group's weight before and after — and whether the available cash covers it. Editing a leg re-renders it; it places nothing.
  options: locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), legs (string matching ^[A-Z]{2,10}:[0-9]{1,9}(\.[0-9]{1,8})?(,[A-Z]{2,10}:[0-9]{1,9}(\.[0-9]{1,8})?){0,4}$), side (one of 'buy', 'sell')
  use when: the user expresses buy or sell INTENT that resolves to a concrete, editable order — including vague intent such as "put ~$10k into semis, keep it diversified". Propose legs through `draft_order`; the impact (weights, cash, shares) is always shown so the consequences are visible before anything is confirmed, and the backend recomputes it on every edit.
  do not use for: placing or confirming an order in prose — nothing here executes, and the ticket says so. A single asset with no impact panel is `order.ticket.v1`; what a proposed sale realises under each lot method is `scenario.comparison.v1`. Never recompute a figure the payload already carries.
- payoff.curve.v1 — Profit and loss of a proposed buy or sell across a bounded range of future prices, entry and break-even marked. An illustrative linear spot payoff, never an options payoff.
  options: fields (list of up to 8 (text), or omit it), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), symbol (one of 'AAVE', 'ARB', 'AVAX', 'BTC', 'ETH', 'LINK', 'SOL', 'USDC'), size (integer 1..1000000000), size_in (one of 'units', 'usd'), side (one of 'buy', 'sell'), range_pct (integer 5..90), steps (integer 1..25)
- portfolio.summary.v1 — The Home hero: total value, the change over a selected period with its direction, a thirty-day sparkline, the owner's greeting, suggested questions for the assistant and the day's top movers.
  options: locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), range (one of '1d', '1w', '1m', 'ytd', '1y', 'all')
- scenario.comparison.v1 — The same proposed sale costed under each lot-selection method, so the realised result and the short/long split can be compared side by side. It marks which column keeps the most after tax, at rates the caller declares and the card prints.
  options: locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), symbol (string matching ^[A-Za-z]{2,10}$, or omit it), quantity (number 0.0..1000000000000.0 or string matching ^(?!^[-+.]*$)[+-]?0*\d*\.?\d{0,8}0*$, or omit it), methods (list of up to 3 (one of 'FIFO', 'LIFO', 'HIFO')), short_term_rate (string matching ^0(\.[0-9]{1,4})?$), long_term_rate (string matching ^0(\.[0-9]{1,4})?$), include_wait (true or false)
  use when: the user faces a choice between strategies and the decision hinges on comparing the same metrics across them — which lots to sell, selling now or waiting. Every column's figures come from this render; never fabricate the comparison.
  do not use for: a single option, where there is nothing to compare — `taxlots.table.v1` shows one sale in detail. Do not rank or bold the values in prose: this card names the spread and recommends no method.
- taxlots.table.v1 — Tax-lot table for a proposed sale: the lots it consumes under FIFO, LIFO or HIFO, each with its holding period, and the realised result split short-term vs long-term. Nothing is traded.
  options: fields (list of up to 8 (text), or omit it), locale (one of 'en-US', 'es-AR', 'de-DE'), precision (integer 0..8), currency (only 'USD'), symbol (string matching ^[A-Za-z]{2,10}$), quantity (string matching ^\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,8})?$), lot_method (one of 'FIFO', 'LIFO', 'HIFO')
  use when: the user asks about selling a position and the answer depends on WHICH lots go — the realised result always splits into its short-term and long-term halves, which is the point of the surface.
  do not use for: comparing several lot-selection methods — `scenario.comparison.v1` puts those side by side. Never estimate a tax rate in prose: this view stops at the realised split, before any rate, fee or wash sale.

renderView.description: Re-render one component of this surface with new declared options. The agent validates `options` against the view's own options model and answers `{componentId, view}`, then an `updateDataModel` at `/<componentId>`; it never asks the model. An undeclared or out-of-range option answers `INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL`.

componentId.description: The component to re-render; its data path.

options.description: The view's declared options, and only those.
